headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill mandates that large energy users, primarily data centers, bear the costs of increasing electric generating capacity and related infrastructure, preventing these costs from being passed to residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, environmental advocates, Dominion Energy.
news_headline: Virginia governor signs Dominion-backed bills, eyes regulators.
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed legislation, including HB 1393, that directs regulators to assign electricity costs to data centers, preventing these costs from being unfairly allocated to residential customers. The bill aims to ensure data centers pay their fair share for energy generation and distribution, though some original provisions for capacity market costs were replaced with broader regulatory authority.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water utilities supplying data centers to report monthly or quarterly water consumption data, including reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board for transparency and oversight.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups (Potomac Conservancy, Friends of the Rappahannock), Senator Kannan Srinivasan, Delegate Liz Guzman.
opponents: Data center industry (implicitly, due to previous lack of transparency).
news_headline: Data centers drinking Potomac River resources, transparency needed.
news_summary: Potomac Conservancy is advocating for SB 553, a bill mandating data centers to report water usage to the State Water Control Board, due to concerns about dwindling groundwater and variable surface water flows. This transparency is crucial for advocating for sustainable infrastructure and combating data center sprawl in the Potomac River region.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill requires data center developers to conduct noise impact assessments near residential areas and schools, and allows localities to require site assessments for impacts on water, agriculture, parks, historic sites, and forests.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Delegate Josh Thomas, Senator Danica Roem, environmental advocates, local communities.
opponents: Data center industry (implicitly, due to added regulations and costs).
news_headline: Virginia's new data center laws address water, noise, siting.
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed several data center bills into law, including those addressing water usage, noise, and site suitability, marking a shift towards regulating the rapidly growing tech facilities. While these are seen as moderate steps, an expert notes that comprehensive reform is still needed, particularly regarding data center subsidies.
